summary: Planned mixed-use block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan, in the 4.8-acre area at 22nd and Illinois Streets that PG&E owns and operates as an electrical switchyard; the D4D's Figure 6.2.3 gives it 85 ft and 125 ft height limits, and its build-out depends on the switchyard's relocation.

milestones.text: Completion expected: Block 13 is in Phase 3 of the revised phasing, and SocketSite's October 2020 schedule table lists its vertical development 2031-2035 (it is not in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list: Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15)
milestones.basis_note: Phase 3 in the October 2020 revised phasing, as reported by SocketSite (Oct 9, 2020), whose 'Re-Phase Program, Detailed Construction Schedule' table lists Block 13 vertical development 2031-2035; a 2020 forecast, not a Block 13-specific commitment, and contingent on the switchyard's relocation ('Ultimate built-out of the PG&E lands ... will depend on the relocation of the switchyard', SF Planning project page).

milestones.text: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero Power Station project and Development Agreement (Ordinance No. 62-20, Board File 200040), the entitlement that first names Block 13 as a development block under the adopted Design for Development's Land Use Table; the Development Agreement's own effective date is May 25, 2020, distinct from the D4D's own February 26, 2020 final-document date

facts.value: Residential, Institutional, Retail, Non-Retail Sales/Services and PDR uses permitted (limited PDR uses at the lowest floors); Laboratory and Life Science uses Not Permitted (D4D final Table 3.1.1)
85 ft and 125 ft (Figure 6.2.3, colour-coded height labels); Standard 6.2.2 lists Block 13 among the midrise buildings (101-145 ft)
One of three blocks (with 1 and 5) eligible to host the project's single permitted district parking garage (max 90 ft, with a publicly accessible rooftop sports field)
The 2024 annual compliance report's only mention of Block 13 is a preservation design-review requirement for its Illinois Street frontage; no building design review or construction is described
Not listed among the six Phase 1 blocks (2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15) named in the 2024 annual compliance report
In the 4.8-acre PG&E-owned northern switchyard area at 22nd and Illinois Streets (the D4D's 'PG&E Sub-area'); the Master Plan's build-out of the PG&E lands depends on relocating the switchyard

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 13; it is not one of the six buildings named in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list (Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15), and no later-phase design review approval was found either.

2026-09-29 audit: an earlier version of this dossier read the '300'MAX' and '280'MAX' labels on Figure 6.2.3 as heights and reported a conflict with Standard 6.2.2; they are dimension lines (plan extents), and the block's heights are 85 ft and 125 ft, within the midrise range. The D4D's Appendix A.12 is titled 'Block 13 Controls (Low-rise Building)' while Standard 6.2.2 lists Block 13 as midrise (101-145 ft); the difference in labels is unexplained.
Block 13's 2031-2035 window comes from a 2020 press table (SocketSite) and is contingent on the PG&E switchyard's relocation; no current Block 13 schedule was found.

DataSF Parcels lists an active addressed lot (4175499, 1101 Illinois St) over this block's approximate footprint; whether it is PG&E's switchyard parcel is not established (owner decision on the geometry).
